_README: PROPOSED permission overlay for unattended agent work. NOT ACTIVE.
An agent cannot write its own broad allowlist -- Claude Code's auto-mode
classifier blocks that, correctly, no matter what was asked for in chat.
So this file is a proposal you apply deliberately:
python3 .claude/hooks/apply_autonomy.py        # merge into .claude/settings.json
or paste the `permissions` block into .claude/settings.json yourself, or add
the entries through /permissions.
WHAT IT DOES. Removes the friction from everything reversible -- running any
research script, any test, any analysis, editing any file outside the frozen
specs, fetching from the primary sources this desk actually cites -- so a
session can work all night without stopping for approvals.
WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO. It does not open the order path. That stays
behind .claude/hooks/guard_order_path.py, because those actions are the ones
that cannot be undone: an order in a closing auction cannot be cancelled after
15:50 ET, the trade phase is not idempotent so a second armed run doubles the
book, and a fill not captured before the TWS restart is gone permanently.
Autonomy is worth a great deal on reversible work and nothing at all on
irreversible work.
TO LIFT THAT TOO, if you decide you want it: delete the PreToolUse block from
.claude/settings.json. Do it knowingly. The alternative, which keeps the
record with a human at no cost to speed, is to let the agent propose the
command and run it yourself with `! <command>` at the prompt.
